description: Figure 8(b) displays the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different methods on the Llama2 model. The x-axis represents the "Co-occurrence Number," plotted on a logarithmic scale with values ranging from $10^1$ to $10^3$. The y-axis shows the "ACC (%)" (accuracy percentage), with a linear scale from 60 to 80. The plot compares six different editing methods: Base (black, solid line with circle markers), MEND (brown, solid line with square markers), MEMIT (purple, solid line with triangle markers), FT (blue, dashed line with triangle markers), IKE (red, dashed line with square markers), and ROME (green, solid line with circle markers). All methods show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases. The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, starting at approximately 72% and reaching about 78%. The MEND method follows, starting at around 66% and reaching about 74%. The MEMIT method starts at approximately 65% and increases to about 73%. The FT method starts at about 64% and increases to around 69%. The IKE method starts at about 64% and increases to approximately 70%. The Base method, representing the LLM without editing, shows the lowest performance, starting at 61% and increasing to about 67%.
